analysis: Examined three files. (1) ProviderLoop+SSEParser.swift: toolCallsDelta and encodeToolCallsForHash changed from OpenAIToolCall to OpenAIToolCallDelta, so streamed tool-call fragments are hashed one marker per fragment in wire order. A complete call encodes as before. This preserves the 'hash commits to what was delivered' property (T-007 area). I found no fail-open path: an encoding failure yields a fixed sentinel, and the parse path is unchanged. Residual: the hash of a fragmented call differs from a hash over a reassembled call. A consumer-side verifier would have to apply the same per-fragment encoding, but that contract is outside the supplied evidence. (2) ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift (lines 1144-1516): new deliveredText accumulates content, reasoning and tool-call name/arguments. It feeds only deliveredCompletionTokenFloor on the cancelled-stream billing path (line 1343). This keeps hash markers from inflating the cancel-time billing floor. Tool-call frames now count as content frames, which stops a late pre-content discard. The provider-side billing floor is provider-reported and was already untrusted to the coordinator. The change does not weaken the inference_complete usage settlement. The v2 cache usage and lookup-receipt flow is unchanged, and the logprobs splice still reads the original frame for hashing. Plaintext SSE is still passed via emitSSE, as before; encryption is handled in the send layer, which is not changed here (T-008 unaffected by this diff). (3) LaunchAgent.swift: two new env keys (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED) are added to the inferencePassthroughEnvKeys allowlist. They are inference-behavior toggles and not secrets. They are only forwarded into the launchd job and do not change privilege. Open questions for integration: that the new behaviors stay default-on as the comment says, that OpenAIToolCallDelta is defined and Codable with stable field names, and the unseen ToolStreamPreparation and ReasoningPromptProbe keys. None of these affects a security conclusion on the supplied evidence.
